source.title_on_document: Who Thinks First? Designing Productive Friction with Engage-to-Unlock GenAI

supplement.where: Included appendices A-E, pp. 26-31. No separately linked external supplement is stated.
supplement.holds: Appendix A: participant demographics (Table 3, p. 26); B: task-duration distributions (Figure 6, p. 27); C: lexical frequency profiles with SEM bands (Figure 7, p. 28); D: assistant system prompts (pp. 26-29); E: a sample conversation transcript (pp. 29-31). The appendices do not contain the discourse contrast differences, standard errors, or confidence intervals announced in the methods on p. 8.

paper_design_summary: Prolific participants wrote a source-based argumentative essay with Human-Only, Standard Chatbot, Engage-to-Unlock, or Time-Matched Unlock access, then judged source-based passages without AI (pp. 5-7, sections 3.1-3.4). Phase 1 randomly assigned people to the first three conditions; all separately recruited Phase 2 participants received Time-Matched Unlock, so comparisons involving that condition are not randomized (p. 6, sections 3.1-3.2; p. 20, section 5.3). Final essays were scored for semantic dispersion, length, and argumentative structure; the AI-only essay corpus was a descriptive reference, and subsequent passage judgments assessed error detection rather than creative production (pp. 7-9, sections 3.3-3.5.3).

studies.label: Argumentative writing and passage evaluation, with two recruitment phases

assignment.what_was_assigned: Phase 1: individual assignment to Human-Only, Standard Chatbot, or Engage-to-Unlock. Phase 2: a separate Prolific cohort, excluding Phase 1 participants, all assigned to Time-Matched Unlock with schedules replayed from Phase 1 Engage-to-Unlock participants. The randomized=yes and online_rct codes apply only to comparisons among the three Phase 1 arms. Phase 2 comparisons are quasi_people/observational and must not be pooled as randomized contrasts. The paper treats both phases as one study (p. 5, section 3; p. 6, sections 3.1-3.2; p. 20, section 5.3).
assignment.quote: In Phase 1, participants were randomly assigned to Human-Only, Standard Chatbot, or Engage-to-Unlock.
assignment.locator: p. 6, section 3.2; also section 3.1, Time-Matched Unlock, and p. 20, section 5.3

arms.name: Human-Only
arms.description: Phase 1 randomized no-assistant condition; shared source readings remained available. Count is analyzed, after attention checks (p. 6, sections 3.1-3.2).

arms.name: Standard Chatbot
arms.description: Phase 1 randomized condition with direct generative Tell-me chatbot access throughout writing. Count is analyzed, after attention checks (p. 6, sections 3.1-3.2).

arms.name: Engage-to-Unlock
arms.description: Phase 1 randomized condition with Teach-me coaching throughout; Tell-me direct generation unlocks after the draft expresses a position and a distinct supporting argumentative development. Participants must choose to switch modes. Count is analyzed, after attention checks (p. 6, sections 3.1-3.2).

arms.name: Time-Matched Unlock
arms.description: Separate, non-randomized Phase 2 cohort. Starts in Teach-me and receives Tell-me availability on a matched Phase 1 participant's elapsed-time schedule, independently of its own writing progress. Count is analyzed, after attention checks (p. 6, sections 3.1-3.2).

participants.exclusions: Of 445 session completers, 398 passed both embedded attention checks and entered the analysis; the paper does not separately print the exclusion total or per-arm pre-exclusion counts (p. 6, section 3.2). Thus 445 is a completer count, not a randomized count, and the analyzed sample should not be called a full intention-to-treat analysis. Six internal pilot sessions were excluded from the main analysis (p. 7, section 3.4). After the attention-check exclusions, participants were retained in their assigned arms, including 14 Time-Matched Unlock participants whose scheduled unlock was not delivered because of a timer error (p. 8, section 3.5.2; p. 11, section 4.1.1).
participants.who: Prolific respondents from the five listed countries. The reported 398 is the combined analyzed sample across both recruitment phases; Phase 1 analyzed arm counts are 99, 98, and 107, and Phase 2 has 94. Assignment-stage counts are not reported (p. 6, section 3.2; p. 26, Table 3).

ai_tool.how_used: Conversational writing assistant with condition-dependent roles: Tell-me permits open-ended ideas, arguments, drafts, and revisions; Teach-me provides process guidance without task-specific arguments or draftable prose. The same model and conversation context underlie both modes. Standard Chatbot has Tell-me from the start; Engage-to-Unlock and Time-Matched Unlock begin with Teach-me and later may gain Tell-me. AI remains available during Task 1 even for those who never unlock direct generation. No AI is available during Task 2 passage evaluation (pp. 5-7, sections 3.1-3.4; pp. 26-29, Appendix D).

task.description: Task 1: write an argumentative essay of at least 200 words about the four-day workweek, using four source summaries with supporting and critical evidence. The writing task is in scope because final essays are compared across writers for semantic similarity/diversity. Task 2: evaluate source-based AI-generated passages for soundness and error type without AI; this is not a creative-production task (p. 7, section 3.3).
task.duration: Each task had a suggested duration of 20 minutes, not enforced; participants could finish at their own pace (p. 7, section 3.4; p. 5, Figure 1).

outcomes.name: Within-condition semantic dispersion and homogenization index of final essays
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Each complete final essay was whitespace-normalized and embedded using Gemini Embedding 2, SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY task type, with 3,072 dimensions. D_c is the mean squared Euclidean distance from essay embeddings to their condition centroid; HI_c = 1 - D_c / D_Human-Only is a transformation of the same outcome, not a separate outcome. There is one dispersion estimate for each of the four participant conditions. The separately generated AI-only reference corpus is descriptive context and is not included in n_units or in the assistance contrasts below. Methods: p. 9, section 3.5.3, equations (1)-(2); results: p. 13, Table 1 and section 4.2.1.

contrasts.reported: Standard Chatbot: n = 98, D_c = 0.188, 95% bootstrap CI [0.178, 0.194], HI_c = -0.050 (-5.0%); Human-Only: n = 99, D_c = 0.179, 95% bootstrap CI [0.167, 0.188], HI_c = 0.000 (baseline). Direction describes the dispersion point estimates only. No formal between-condition difference or equivalence test is reported.

diversity_detail.metric: D_c: mean squared Euclidean distance to the within-condition centroid. HI_c = 1 - D_c / D_Human-Only. Higher D_c means greater diversity; higher HI_c means greater homogenization.
diversity_detail.embedding_model: Gemini Embedding 2; SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY task type; 3,072-dimensional vectors (p. 9, section 3.5.3).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each final essay is compared with the centroid of all final essays in its own condition, and squared distances are averaged within that condition. This compares different writers, not the variety of ideas inside one essay (p. 9, equations (1)-(2)).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Condition-level 95% percentile bootstrap confidence intervals from 5,000 resamples. The precise bootstrap resampling procedure is not further specified. No standard error or confidence interval for an arm difference is printed, and the paper explicitly does not use these intervals as formal tests of between-condition differences or equivalence (p. 9, section 3.5.3; p. 13, Table 1).
diversity_detail.notes: The contrast direction uses D_c, for which higher is more diverse. The printed HI_c values are preserved without sign changes or recomputation; their interpretation must be reversed when expressing a diversity benefit. Table 1 values are rounded, so HI_c should not be recomputed from the printed D_c values. The AI-only reference has n = 100 essays, D_c = 0.065, 95% bootstrap CI [0.061, 0.068], HI_c = +0.636 (+63.6%); this is an ancillary AI-versus-human output comparison, not an assistance effect or an additional group of people (p. 8, section 3.5.3; p. 13, Table 1). The paper explicitly distinguishes PCA semantic location from diversity (p. 9).

outcomes.name: Final-essay word count
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of words in each participant's final essay; one essay per participant. Retained as an elaboration/length measure, not a rating of creativity or writing quality. Continuous outcomes are analyzed at participant level (p. 8, sections 3.5.1 and 3.5.3). Means and SDs below use the more precise values printed in section 4.2.3 on p. 14; Table 2 on p. 15 rounds them to one decimal place. No pairwise word-count statistics are printed.

outcomes.name: Total discourse elements in the final essay
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: An LLM-based discourse classifier counts argumentative/discourse elements in each final essay. This is an amount-of-argumentation measure, not the number of separately generated creative ideas or a creativity rating. Discourse categories are Lead, Position, Claim, Counterclaim, Rebuttal, Evidence, and Concluding Statement (p. 6, section 3.1). The classifier's underlying model is not specified. Discourse analyses use one essay per participant (p. 8, section 3.5.3).

contrasts.reported: Mean counts: Engage-to-Unlock 9.66, Standard Chatbot 9.71, Human-Only 8.30, Time-Matched Unlock 9.16. The exploratory ordinary four-condition ANOVA is F(3, 394) = 4.66, p = .003. The text states that planned contrasts for outcomes other than counterclaims were not statistically significant. No numeric pairwise difference, SE, CI, p-value, or arm SD is printed for total discourse elements.

eligibility.reason: Phase 1 randomly assigned people to Human-Only, Standard Chatbot, or Engage-to-Unlock, including both assistance-versus-no-assistance and AI-configuration contrasts (p. 6, sections 3.1-3.2). The analyzed counts in these arms are 99, 98, and 107, so the qualifying randomized sample clearly exceeds 50 people; the complete two-phase study analyzed 398 people (p. 6, section 3.2; p. 26, Table 3). Final essays have a computed cross-writer semantic-dispersion outcome, meeting the writing-diversity scope even though creativity was not rated (p. 9, section 3.5.3; p. 13, Table 1). Only Phase 1 contrasts support core eligibility. Comparisons with Time-Matched Unlock are non-randomized, and comparisons with the AI-only reference are context evidence, not additional randomized arms (p. 8, section 3.5.3; p. 20, section 5.3). The absence of a reported formal dispersion contrast test does not negate study eligibility; no contrast SE is supplied for pooling.

one_line_finding: Among 398 analyzed people, essay semantic dispersion was descriptively similar across Human-Only (0.179), Engage-to-Unlock (0.187), Standard Chatbot (0.188), and Time-Matched Unlock (0.188), with no formal between-condition dispersion test reported (p. 6, section 3.2; p. 13, Table 1; p. 9, section 3.5.3).
open_questions: Methods promise discourse mean differences, standard errors, degrees of freedom, and confidence intervals (p. 8, section 3.5.3), but these are not printed in the results on p. 15 or the included appendices; no external supplement or data/code link is supplied. Arm-level SDs and contrast precision for these outcomes remain unavailable.

The study-level schema has one design_class, but the paper contains randomized Phase 1 and non-randomized Phase 2 comparisons. Any extraction must preserve the per-contrast restriction recorded here (p. 6, section 3.1; p. 20, section 5.3).
notes: The entire markdown, including references and appendices A-E, was read. PDF text was checked for the design, counts, measures, reported statistics, and cited tables/figures. One study is recorded because the paper presents one two-phase experiment; the AI-only corpus is an ancillary reference, not an additional participant study, and the internal pilots and classifier validation are not independent eligible experiments. The semantic-dispersion outcome alone establishes the output criterion; the remaining recorded outcomes preserve the essay elaboration and argumentative-structure measures without treating them as validated creativity ratings. Discourse category diversity is within an essay, not diversity across people. All recorded outcomes come from Task 1, when AI was available in the AI arms; availability is not equivalent to actual generation use. Task 2 was after AI removal, but its passage evaluation accuracy and efficiency concern error detection in supplied passages, not creativity or diversity of participants' own creative output, so no after_ai creativity outcome is entered (p. 7, section 3.3). PCA semantic location is expressly distinguished from diversity (p. 9, section 3.5.3; p. 12, Figure 2; p. 14, section 4.2.1). Lexical frequency profiles and source/AI text reuse are explanatory composition measures rather than creativity scores or dispersion across writers and are not counted as additional eligible outcomes (p. 9, section 3.5.3; pp. 13-15, sections 4.1.2 and 4.2.2, Table 2; p. 28, Figure 7). Prompt counts, time, clipboard actions, and subjective reports are also outside this outcome inventory. No creativity or novelty ratings, delayed creative-production assessment, preregistration, or public data/code repository is stated. No effect sizes, differences, standard errors, exclusion totals, or phase totals were calculated.
